title: Starter usage staircase — quick guesstimates
content:
Top-level goal: very rough numbers to validate a simple starter plan that graduates users along a 'usage staircase' (free -> starter -> growth). Not final, just a back-of-envelope to feed the deck and an initial A/B test.

KEY PREMISES / ASSUMPTIONS (feel free to challenge):
- Redwood hosted marginal model cost to us (avg across small models + infra amort): $0.0009 per 1k tokens (conservative low-end estimate).
- Network + storage + infra overhead per session: ~ $0.03 amortized if session lasts > 30s (we'll account separately).
- Avg token usage per active user per month (AUPM): scenario-based (see below).
- Conversion from free -> paid: 2.5% baseline (optimistic), can widen with product hooks.
- CAC for starter tier from self-serve: $45 (paid ads + onboarding friction amortized).
- Churn (monthly) starter: 8% assumed; growth tier better (5%).

SCENARIOS (AUPM = avg tokens per active monthly user):
1) Casual app (chat-like, ~1500 tokens/session * 3 sessions/month -> 4500 tokens AUPM)
   - token cost per user = 4.5 * $0.0009 = $0.00405 (~0.4 cents)
   - infra/session overhead (3 sessions) = $0.09
   - total opex/user/month ≈ $0.094
   - price point candidate: Starter monthly $4.99 incl 50k tokens? (overkill).
   - margin check: huge margin; issue is perception of value vs price.

2) Power user (multi-step workflows, 12k tokens/month)
   - token cost = 12 * $0.0009 = $0.0108 (~1.1 cents)
   - infra overhead ~ $0.12 (assume 8 short sessions)
   - opex/user/month ≈ $0.1308
   - price candidate: $9.99/month with 200k token cap + throttled overage.

3) Embedding-heavy analytics user (API calls, 250k tokens + embedding calls):
   - token cost = 250 * $0.0009 = $0.225
   - embeddings (indexing) cost estimate: $0.03 per 1k embed-usage units -> assume $0.15
   - infra + storage = $0.50 (index storage amortized)
   - total opex/month ≈ $0.905
   - price candidate: custom / dedicated or pay-as-you-go; not in starter.

STARTER PLAN: thinking checklist
- Price: $4.99/mo or $49/yr (discounted)
- Included: 50K tokens / mo + 2k embed units (rough) + basic support
- Overage: $0.50 per 50k tokens (packaged micro-buckets) or per-token at $0.010/1k (experiment)
- Rationale: keep price psychologically low to reduce barrier while letting >~5k AUPM users naturally convert.

Quick unit-econ for starter plan (best-effort):
- ARR per converting user (monthly $4.99): 4.99 * 12 = $59.88
- Gross margin (approx): price - opex (use scenario 1 as typical starter usage) -> 59.88 - (0.094*12) = 59.88 - 1.128 = 58.75/year -> ~98% gross margin (model cost tiny).
- Payback on CAC: CAC $45 -> ~0.77 years (~9 months) at baseline churn. Acceptable for self-serve.

GRADUATION / USAGE STAIRCASE FLOW (how users move up):
- Free tier: 2k tokens / mo, up to 3 sessions, low-quality model variant -> converts when users hit cap and see value.
- Starter tier ($4.99): 50k tokens, higher concurrency, higher-quality model + small embedding credits.
- Growth tier ($49/mo): 500k tokens + advanced features (routing control, longer context, export).
- Auto-upgrade triggers: 3 consecutive months >80% quota -> prompt in-app + email 1-click upgrade.

NOTES ON OVERAGE DESIGN (important):
- Micro-buckets are less scary than per-token math. e.g., 50k token top-up = $0.50 or $2? Need to test price sensitivity.
- Alternatively, throttle performance (slower response / model fallback) after quota to nudge upgrade. Might be lower friction / cheaper.

SENSITIVITY: what breaks this?
- If our true marginal model cost is 5x higher (e.g., $0.0045/1k), starter economics still okay, but embeddings and heavy API users become loss-making unless we push them to Dedicated.
- If conversion < 1% CAC payback goes >2yrs; need better organic hooks.

TESTS / EXPERIMENTS TO RUN (short list):
- A/B test starter price $3.99 vs $4.99 pop-up after hitting free threshold (track conversion within 30 days). (JIRA: JIRA-3271).
- Offer first-month discount $1 to reduce CAC payback; measure retention delta.
- Test overage as micro-buckets vs per-token on checkout flow. (Slack thread: #pricing-discuss).

OPEN QUESTIONS / TODOs:
- Reconcile our internal per-1k token cost with infra teams (ask infra-costs@redwood) — I think current $/1k is under-estimated.
- How do we account for KV cache hits (saves tokens): add separate optimistic scenario where 20% token saved -> increases margin.
- Experiment idea: tiered latency SLAs for starter vs growth (affects infra cost).

RANDOM NOTES / brain dumps:
- Could bundle small amounts of compute credits (e.g., 100 inference credits) that translate to priority queueing on Dedicated pools for a month — gives perceived premium without big cost.
- Yearly plan anchor: $49/yr vs $4.99/mo improves LTV by ~20% (less churn).
- Consider metered trial: give credit $5 to spend on any model; shows true value.

SHORT ACTION ITEMS (for me):
- Sync with infra on actual marginal token + session cost (tag Ethan).
- Draft A/B test PR for $3.99 vs $4.99 popup with KPIs (conversion, churn at 30/90d).
- Put a short experiment plan into Confluence Pricing Board.

If anyone reads: shout if you have alternate cost inputs or better CAC numbers — these numbers are intentionally fuzzy.

[end of scratchpad]
